- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for rebound potential.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction: if price spiked 3%+ in last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, increase forecast by 1–2% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model tends to lag; apply 1–2 day delay in price adjustment.
